rules.title: Account holds a privilege that leads to SYSTEM
rules.subject: {name}
rules.why: These privileges get around access checks. SeImpersonate and SeAssignPrimaryToken can turn a coerced SYSTEM authentication into a SYSTEM process; SeBackup and SeRestore read and write any file; SeDebug opens any process; SeTakeOwnership takes any object; SeLoadDriver loads kernel code. A privilege listed as Disabled can still be enabled by the account itself. Service accounts (IIS, SQL Server) often hold SeImpersonate, so compromising the service compromises the machine.
rules.fix: Remove the right under Local Security Policy > User Rights Assignment (or by GPO) unless the account really needs it. For services, use virtual or managed service accounts and keep the service patched.

rules.title: Account is in an admin-equivalent group
rules.subject: {name}
rules.why: Backup Operators can read and write any file, registry hives included; Server Operators and Account Operators can change services and accounts; Hyper-V Administrators control VMs and their disks; DnsAdmins can make the DNS service load a DLL. Each is a short path to SYSTEM or domain admin.
rules.fix: Remove the membership unless the account really needs it, and treat remaining members as administrators.

rules.title: Account can control the Docker engine
rules.subject: {name}
rules.why: Members of docker-users can drive the Docker engine, which runs with high privileges. Depending on the backend and its settings, a container can be given access to host files, so membership should be treated as admin-equivalent.
rules.fix: Only add people who are already administrators to docker-users, and remove anyone who doesn't use Docker.
